controls: JAR Sound Compensation Table (Coolant Temperature) — JAR Sound = Piston Slap. These tables are used to retard ignition timing to prevent damage from occuring. I'd recommend using the Coolant Compensation Table for the MBT calculation instead. This value is subtracted from the Engine RPM Table value (below) to set vADVJAR. This value is subtracted from the timing value, so raising these values will cause the timing to be retarded. This value is ALWAYS USED to calculate timing (apart from idle and decel).

JAR Sound Compensation Table (Engine RPM) — JAR Sound = Piston Slap. These tables are used to retard ignition timing to prevent damage from occuring. I'd recommend using the main Ignition Timing Maps to compensate for RPM instead. This value has the mTADVC1 Table value subtracted from it before setting vADVJAR. So if you want these tables to compensate, you need to have this value be larger than the Coolant Comp value. Since the value gets subtracted, THESE VALUES CANNOT BE BELOW 0! If they're below 0, it'll just set the value to 0.

controls: JAR Sound Compensation Table (Coolant Temperature) — JAR Sound = Piston Slap. These tables are used to retard ignition timing to prevent damage from occuring. I'd recommend using the Coolant Compensation Table for the MBT calculation instead. This value is subtracted from the Engine RPM Table value (below) to set vADVJAR. This value is subtracted from the timing value, so raising these values will cause the timing to be retarded. This value is ALWAYS USED to calculate timing (apart from idle and decel).

JAR Sound Compensation Table (Engine RPM) — JAR Sound = Piston Slap. These tables are used to retard ignition timing to prevent damage from occuring. I'd recommend using the main Ignition Timing Maps to compensate for RPM instead. This value has the mTADVC1 Table value subtracted from it before setting vADVJAR. So if you want these tables to compensate, you need to have this value be larger than the Coolant Comp value. Since the value gets subtracted, THESE VALUES CANNOT BE BELOW 0! If they're below 0, it'll just set the value to 0.

I'd recommend using the main Ignition Timing Maps to compensate for RPM instead. This value has the mTADVC1 Table value subtracted from it before setting vADVJAR. So if you want these tables to compensate, you need to have this value be larger than the Coolant Comp value. Since the value gets subtracted, THESE VALUES CANNOT BE BELOW 0! controls: Individual Cylinder Fuel Trims — "Compensation value table by the cylinder". This adds or subtracts fuel from the respective cylinder. Values over 100 add fuel, values under 100 subtract fuel.

MAF Table — Inhalation air quantity conversion table. This table represents airflow through the MAF sensor at a given voltage. For stock MAF diameter intakes, I'd strongly recommend utilizing the MAF Factor alongside Fuel Compensation to dial in your fueling, rather than utilizing this table.

Load Base Fuel Schedule Table — The 100% BFS value based on RPM used to calculate "Calculated Load"0. This table is primarily used for vehicles equipped with an automatic transmission. You want to ensure that your calculated load parameter is reading 100% at WOT at all times. Since this value is the 100% value, all you need to do is lower each RPM's 100% BFS value until your WOT BFS exceeds this value.

Cranking Base Fuel Schedule Table — Sets the cranking BFS. This table value is still compensated by the Fuel Compensation Map, so you can use that map to further dial in cranking fueling. During cranking, the K-Value is not utilized. So you'll have to adjust this table whenever you modify your fueling system (i.e. larger injectors).

So if you want these tables to compensate, you need to have this value be larger than the Coolant Comp value. Since the value gets subtracted, THESE VALUES CANNOT BE BELOW 0! This value is subtracted from the timing value, so raising these values will cause the timing to be retarded. This value is ALWAYS USED to calculate timing (apart from idle and decel).

I'd recommend using the main Ignition Timing Maps to compensate for RPM instead. This value has the mTADVC1 Table value subtracted from it before setting vADVJAR. So if you want these tables to compensate, you need to have this value be larger than the Coolant Comp value. Since the value gets subtracted, THESE VALUES CANNOT BE BELOW 0! JAR Sound Compensation Table (Coolant Temperature) — JAR Sound = Piston Slap. These tables are used to retard ignition timing to prevent damage from occuring. I'd recommend using the Coolant Compensation Table for the MBT calculation instead. This value is subtracted from the Engine RPM Table value (below) to set vADVJAR. This value is subtracted from the timing value, so raising these values will cause the timing to be retarded. This value is ALWAYS USED to calculate timing (apart from idle and decel).

JAR Sound Compensation Table (Engine RPM) — JAR Sound = Piston Slap. These tables are used to retard ignition timing to prevent damage from occuring. I'd recommend using the main Ignition Timing Maps to compensate for RPM instead. This value has the mTADVC1 Table value subtracted from it before setting vADVJAR. So if you want these tables to compensate, you need to have this value be larger than the Coolant Comp value. Since the value gets subtracted, THESE VALUES CANNOT BE BELOW 0! If they're below 0, it'll just set the value to 0.

controls: Cold Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when coolant temperature hasn't breached the proper threshold. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well.
axes: X axis: Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency @ 0xBAB0; Y axis: Engine Speed @ 0xBAC0

controls: Cold Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing.
values_mean: Knock Window (0: Off | 1: On), raw value
axes: X axis: Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency @ 0xBAB0; Y axis: Engine Speed @ 0xBAC0

controls: High Detonation Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-detonation is occurring. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. Make sure that this map's values are lower than the high octane map's values.
axes: X axis: Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency @ 0xBAB0; Y axis: Engine Speed @ 0xBAC0

controls: High Detonation Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing.
values_mean: Knock Window (0: Off | 1: On), raw value
axes: X axis: Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency @ 0xBAB0; Y axis: Engine Speed @ 0xBAC0

controls: Fuel Compensation Map (16x16) — This map will directly trim Base Fuel Schedule. Given how we have transient throttle fuel compensation maps, this map is really designed for steady state conditions with little RPM deviance. However, you can use this map to tune for transient conditions. View it similarly to STFT's in a way. But as a preset trimming value rather than reacting to AFR deviances.
axes: X axis: QH0 Flow Quantity @ 0xB98A; Y axis: Engine Speed @ 0xB94E

controls: Target AFR Map (8x8) — This map will be directly influence fueling. Any cells that are set to 14.7 AFR will have the ECU run in closed-loop mode. (Obviously excluding decel) This map will not guarantee that your targets are hit, so you will need to adjust your fueling elsewhere to ensure you're hitting your targets.

Bosch Fuel Cut Table — "BOSCH cut speed table" This is the fuel cut table used for Bosch ECU's only. If the RPM's are above the cut speed, then fuel cut will occur (on decel) until the RPM's hit the recover speed.

JECS Fuel Cut Table — "JECS cut speed table" This is the fuel cut table used for JECS/Hitachi ECU's only. If the RPM's are above the cut speed, then fuel cut will occur (on decel) until the RPM's hit the recover speed.
